name: Zhili clique
alt: Cao Kun and Wu Peifu's regime

predecessors.name: Anhui clique
predecessors.text: Beijing and Zhili, whose central government the Anhui clique lost in the Zhili-Anhui War of 14-23 July 1920

successors.name: Kuomintang (Guangzhou and Nanjing Nationalist government)
successors.text: Wu Peifu's and Sun Chuanfang's provinces taken by the National Revolutionary Army, 1926-1927

successors.name: Fengtian clique
successors.text: Zhili's northern provinces, lost in November 1924 'to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun'

ledger.x: 1920: the Zhili clique wins the capital.

1922 (bridging): the Zhili page says only that the clique 'consolidated its control over Henan' and 'At its height, it also controlled Jiangsu, Jiangxi, and Hubei', with no dates; the year is the researcher's reading of the 1922 victory.
April 1922: the First Zhili-Fengtian War.

18 June 1922: Zhili victory; the peace was signed aboard a British warship off Qinhuangdao; 'Shanhaiguan subsequently became the border between the two cliques'; Wu Peifu's armies 'took control of the central government in Beijing'.
1922: Rehe, Chahar and Suiyuan come under Zhili control.

By the summer of 1924 (bridging): the Anhui clique page says 'all their provinces were eventually annexed by the Zhili clique by the summer of 1924' (re-read 2026-10-25) and dates only Fujian (March 1924) and Zhejiang and Shanghai (12 October 1924); Anhui province itself is not named as lost, so the year is the page's…
March 1924: Fujian.
3 September 1924: the Jiangsu-Zhejiang War.
15 September 1924: the Second Zhili-Fengtian War begins.
12 October 1924: the war 'ended on 12 October 1924 with an Anhui defeat'.
October 1924: Zhejiang and Shanghai are Zhili's after the Jiangsu-Zhejiang War (Anhui defeat on 12 October 1924); Lu Yongxiang's Zhejiang army and He Fenglin's Shanghai were the Anhui clique's.
22 October 1924: Feng Yuxiang's Beijing Coup takes the capital from the Zhili clique.
3 November 1924: the Second Zhili-Fengtian War ends; Wu Peifu left Tianjin by sea.
November 1924 (bridging): the war ends with 'a Zhili loss of all of its northern provinces to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun'; the page does not name Chahar or Suiyuan.
November 1924: Zhili's north falls.
November 1924 (bridging): Rehe goes with the rest of Zhili's north, to Fengtian by the reviewer's split.

1925 (bridging): the Northern Expedition page lists 'Wu Peifu: Held northern Hunan, Hubei, and Henan in 1926'; how and when Wu came to hold northern Hunan is not on the pages opened, and 'nobody' stands for the several Hunan authorities.
By August 1925: Jiangsu and Anhui are the Fengtian Army's.
25 November 1925: Sun Chuanfang is again master of Jiangsu.
22 August 1926: Hunan falls.
10 October 1926: Wuchang surrenders.
9 November 1926: the NRA 'by 9 November 1926, retook control of Nanchang'; Jiangxi is Sun Chuanfang's in the page's 1926 snapshot.
9 December 1926: 'He Yingqin's forces entered Fuzhou on 9 December 1926.'
By 23 February 1927: 'Zhejiang was under complete KMT control by 23 February 1927.'
22 March 1927: 'on 22 March 1927, Bai's forces marched into Shanghai victorious.'
28 May 1927: the Guominjun takes Luoyang and, with it, Henan.
Late August 1927: the last Zhili army falls.

wars.name: Zhili-Anhui War
wars.outcome: Zhili and Fengtian victory: the Anhui clique was destroyed and Duan Qirui resigned on 19 July 1920.

wars.name: First Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Zhili victory; Fengtian retreated to Manchuria and Shanhaiguan became the border.

wars.name: First Jiangsu-Zhejiang War
wars.outcome: Zhili victory: Zhejiang and Shanghai taken from the Anhui clique; the war 'ended on 12 October 1924 with an Anhui defeat'.

wars.name: Second Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Zhili defeat: Feng Yuxiang's coup and the Fengtian advance cost Zhili all its northern provinces.

wars.name: Anti-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Fengtian and Zhili victory (infobox): the Guominjun was driven from Tianjin and Beijing; 'Zhang and Wu jointly occupied Beijing'.

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Kuomintang victory: Hunan (22 August 1926), Hubei (10 October), Jiangxi (9 November), Fuzhou (9 December), Zhejiang (23 February 1927), Shanghai (22 March) and Sun Chuanfang's defeat at Longtan in late August 1927.

certainty.note: Provincial control by garrison commanders; the pages give no boundaries other than whole provinces, and the clique's grip on each province changed with the wars.
